meta.title: Learning path: five games, one mechanic at a time

database.label: Help you can open any time

nodes.label: 4 · Read the Chain
nodes.sublabel: OI walls, PCR, max pain, skew

cards.title: 1 · NIFTY Weekly
items: An option is the right to buy (CE, call) or sell (PE, put) NIFTY at a set price, the strike. You never have to use it.
The premium you pay is the most you can lose.
Time value melts a little every trading day until Tuesday expiry.
India VIX, the market's expected swing, moves option prices.
You buy at the ask and sell at the bid; the gap costs you.
Charges: ₹20 brokerage per order, STT 0.15% on sells, plus small fees and GST.

cards.title: 2 · Payoff Painter
items: A payoff diagram shows profit or loss in ₹ per lot (65 units) at expiry.
Breakeven = strike + premium for a call, strike − premium for a put.
A buyer's loss stops at the premium; a seller's loss has no cap.
Level 2: spreads (buy one option, sell another) set both the risk and the reward.

cards.title: 3 · Expiry Tuesday
items: 0DTE = zero days to expiry: trading on Tuesday itself.
An out-of-the-money (OTM) option is pure time value and goes to ₹0 by 15:30.
Cheap is not good: a ₹5 option is cheap because it will probably expire worthless.
Theta (time decay) now counts per hour; gamma makes prices jump as NIFTY nears the strike.

cards.title: 4 · Read the Chain
items: ATM (at the money) is the strike closest to NIFTY's current level.
Big open interest (OI) at a strike acts as a wall: support below, resistance above.
PCR (put-call ratio) and max pain (where option buyers lose most) read the crowd.
Put skew: downside puts cost more than equally distant calls.
Delta ≈ the chance the option ends in the money.

cards.title: 5 · Seller's Week
items: The seller receives the premium up front and keeps it if the option expires worthless.
Selling blocks margin, about ₹1.25 lakh per NIFTY lot.
MTM (mark to market): profit or loss is settled every day.
A gap day opens far from yesterday's close, past any stop.
Buying a further-out option turns the sale into a credit spread with a known worst case.

cards.title: Finish line
items: You can explain why an option's price moves: the NIFTY level, time left, and VIX.
And why SEBI found that 91% of retail F&O (futures and options) traders lost money in FY25.
